newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indian oilseeds output, meal exports seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Indian oilseeds output, meal exports seen rising.

text.p: India's oilseeds production is seen rising to 38 million tonnes in 2002 from the current 30 million tonnes, an official of the Soybean Processors Association of India said on Monday.
B.V. Mehta said at a feed ingredients conference in Singapore that oilmeal exports by India will also increase to six million tonnes from 4.35 million tonnes in the 1996/97 April/March season.
Most of India's oilmeal exports go to South Korea, Thailand, Malaysia, Japan, Indonesia and the Philippines.

"At present, these markets account for close to 60 percent of the country's aggregate exports," Mehta said. He predicted that oilseed imports into India are "imminent (and) would make the processing industry more vibrant, more competitive and more export-oriented."
But some problems plague the oilmeal industry in India, the official said. This includes an acute shortage of rail wagons which forces exporters to use more expensive road transport.

Facilities at Indian ports like Bedi, Bhavnagar and Kakinada, which handle nearly 80 percent of export shipments "are largely outdated and inefficient. All these mean that India's shipping costs are rather high," Mehta added.
There are also no hedging facilities in the country at the moment although a domestic futures exchange will probably open in two years to help exporters in this matter.
